1. (Currently amended) A method, comprising: inputting database constructs generated by a database optimizer as an input to a trained machine-learning algorithm __that has been trained on historical database performance data collected from a plurality of different database systems__; obtaining a database operation predictor from the machine-learning algorithm as an output; modifying at least one of the database constructs based on the database operation predictor producing a modified database construct; and processing a database operation with the database constructs and the modified database construct.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein inputting further includes inputting the database constructs as query execution plans for a query __and wherein the machine-learning algorithm is trained to predict performance metrics not directly provided by the database optimizer__.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein inputting further includes identifying at least one database construct as a least cost query execution plan identified from the query execution plans by the database optimizer __and providing alternative query execution plans to the machine-learning algorithm for comparative analysis__.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein identifying further includes identifying individual pieces of the least cost query execution plan as: a total number of spools used, cardinality for tables with any intermediate results used, a total number of merge joins, a total number of hash joins, nested loop joins, references for the spools, and costs per database resource assigned by the database optimizer __and wherein the machine-learning algorithm generates predictions based on patterns across these individual pieces that differ from the optimizer's cost model__.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein obtaining further includes acquiring the database operation predictor as an estimated Central Process Unit (CPU) execution time for one or more Access Module Processors to execute when processing the database operation __that is predicted by the machine-learning algorithm independent of the database optimizer's CPU cost estimates__.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein obtaining further includes acquiring the database operation predictor as an estimated number of Input/Output (I/O) operations performed by one or more Access Module Processors during execution when processing the database operation __that is predicted by the machine-learning algorithm independent of the database optimizer's I/O cost estimates__.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein modifying further includes changing a scheduled execution time for the database operation as the modified database construct __based on the database operation predictor indicating that actual execution time will differ from the optimizer's estimate by a threshold amount__.

8. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein modifying further includes changing a scheduled execution time for execution of a query as the modified database construct __based on the database operation predictor indicating that actual execution time will differ from the optimizer's estimate by a threshold amount__.

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein modifying further includes changing a workgroup assigned to the database operation as the modified database construct __based on the database operation predictor indicating resource contention or performance degradation not accounted for by the database optimizer__.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1 further comprising, storing the database operation predictor in database statistics associated with the database operation and the database constructs __along with metadata indicating the source of the prediction as the machine-learning algorithm rather than the database optimizer__.

12. (Currently amended) A method comprising: training a machine-learning algorithm with database constructs produced by a database optimizer __and actual observed execution metrics from prior query executions that differ from the optimizer's predicted metrics__; receiving query execution plans for a query from the database optimizer with a least cost query execution plan identified by the database optimizer for the query; providing the query execution plans as input to the machine-learning algorithm; obtaining as an output a predicted execution time for the query based on the least cost query execution plan __wherein the predicted execution time is generated by the machine-learning algorithm using learned patterns that differ from the optimizer's cost model__; and modifying one of: the least cost query execution plan for the query, a scheduled execution time for the query, and resources that are used to execute the query based on the predicted execution time.

15. (Currently amended) The method of claim 12, wherein providing further includes providing the database tool within a workload scheduler and management component of a database system __that integrates the machine-learning algorithm's predictions with workload scheduling decisions__.

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 12, wherein training further includes training the machine-learning algorithm as a linear regression-based machine-learning algorithm __that learns coefficients for database construct features based on historical execution data__.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 12, wherein modifying further includes changing an execution resource of the least cost query execution plan based on the predicted query execution time and a current performance associated with the execution resource __wherein the change is made when the predicted execution time indicates a Service Level Agreement violation that would not be predicted by the database optimizer alone__.

19. (Currently amended) A system, comprising: a database management system; at least one hardware processor; a non-transitory computer-readable storage medium having executable instructions representing a trained machine-learning algorithm __trained on historical database performance data from a plurality of different database systems__; the machine learning algorithm configured to execute on the at least one hardware processor from the non-transitory computer-readable storage medium and to perform processing to: i) receive as input database constructs produced by a database optimizer for a database operation of the database management system; and ii) provide as output a predicted value relevant to one of: one or more of the database constructs and the database operation __wherein the predicted value is generated using learned patterns that differ from the database optimizer's cost model__; wherein the database management system is configured to process the predicted value to determine whether to modify one of: the one or more database constructs and the database operation before processing the database operation within the database management system.

20. (Currently amended) The system of claim 19, wherein the predicted value is an estimated query execution time for a query __predicted by the machine-learning algorithm independent of the database optimizer's estimates__ and the database operation is execution of a query execution plan for the query within the database management system.
